findings.body:
**Enforce the drain deadline during systemd observations.**

`_wait_drain()` has a 15-second default budget, but `_jobs()` can spend 30 seconds on its first query. If that query returns after 20 seconds, the loop still makes the remaining queries. It can also report success before it checks the expired deadline.

Pass the remaining budget to each observation. Refuse when the budget is exhausted, including before accepting a successful sample.
findings.title: Enforce the drain deadline during systemd observations.

findings.body:
**Keep completion-log failures from blocking rollback.**

If `completion()` rejects a malformed or oversized log, the controller calls `stop_and_drain()` again before `restore()` (`deploy-controller.py:2117–2121`). The adapter can establish a safe fence, then reject the same log at Line 933. The controller never reaches `restore()`, and the service remains masked.

Read the completion baseline on the forward switch path, not as a prerequisite for the rollback fence. Invalid evidence must still block installation, and live or unknown ownership must still block restoration.
findings.title: Keep completion-log failures from blocking rollback.

findings.body:
**Validate the effective fixture units before fencing.**

A `crq-tick.timer` drop-in from another user unit-load directory can change which service the timer triggers without changing the local timer file or its `FragmentPath`. The inventory accepts that configuration. The release check then accepts an active, loaded timer, but the controller waits for a second tick completion that the timer cannot provide. ([freedesktop.org](https://freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.unit.html?utm_source=openai))

Check the effective fragment, drop-in paths, and trigger target for each declared unit. Permit the declared repair drop-in and refuse unexpected overrides before mutation.
findings.title: Validate the effective fixture units before fencing.

findings.body:
**Do not use truncated command output to prove job absence.**

If `list-jobs` returns more than 8,000 characters, Line 154 drops the leading rows. A waiting job for `crq-repair.path` in those rows never reaches `_jobs_for()`. If the path is still inactive and the other drain checks pass, `_wait_drain()` reports success with that job still queued.

Filter the query to the owned units and require complete output for the absence check. Keep truncation for diagnostics, not for the data the check consumes. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Do not use truncated command output to prove job absence.

findings.body:
**Use defaults only for ports that were not supplied.**

A fake `SystemdPort` whose `__len__` reports pending jobs is false when it has no jobs. `production_adapter` discards it and supplies a real `SubprocessSystemd`, even if the caller supplied a fake journal source. Later adapter calls can reach the real user manager. Use `is None` for each default so an injected port stays bound regardless of its truth value.
findings.title: Use defaults only for ports that were not supplied.

findings.body:
**Reject dependencies that propagate the fence stop to another unit.**

If `ingress.service` has `[Unit] StopPropagatedFrom=crq-tick.service`, discovery ignores the directive. The fence can then stop the active co-tenant when it stops `crq-tick.service`. Systemd v257 also supports the forward form, `PropagatesStopTo=`. Include both directives in the dependency scan. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/257/systemd.unit.html))
findings.title: Reject dependencies that propagate the fence stop to another unit.

findings.body:
**Enforce the scan bound before materializing child entries.**

`list(entry.iterdir())` collects every child of a `.wants` or `.requires` directory before the recursive scan checks `MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES`. The declared drop-in check also sorts all entries before checking the permitted names. A large directory can consume memory and delay refusal before the bound takes effect. Enumerate incrementally and refuse on overflow. For declared drop-ins, the first unexpected name is enough to refuse.






Also applies to: 547-547
findings.title: Enforce the scan bound before materializing child entries.

findings.body:
**Resolve or refuse specifiers that can conceal an activation target.**

In `ingress-crq.socket`, `[Socket] Service=%j-tick.service` resolves to `crq-tick.service` in systemd v257. The binding leaves `%j` unchanged, so `CRQ_NAME_RE` does not find the target and discovery can accept the socket. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/257/systemd.unit.html))

Match systemd's expansion for dependency targets. If the binding cannot resolve a specifier in this scope, refuse the observation rather than reporting it as supported. Keep literal and correctly resolved targets subject to the same check.
findings.title: Resolve or refuse specifiers that can conceal an activation target.

findings.body:
**Bound the number of retained dependency diagnostics.**

Each matching directive adds a new string to `foreign`. Hundreds of individually in-bound files with repeated `Wants=crq-tick.service` directives can retain millions of strings before discovery returns. Cap the diagnostic sample and keep scanning within the existing limits. The adapter will still refuse because `foreign` is nonempty, and an unreadable later file can still make `complete` false.
findings.title: Bound the number of retained dependency diagnostics.

findings.body:
**Document resolved cgroup containment, not a ban on symlink components.**

If `service-a` is a symlink to `service-b` under the same cgroup root, `cgroup_pids()` resolves the link and can read `service-b/cgroup.procs`. It rejects a resolved path outside the root and checks the final `cgroup.procs` for a symlink. It also drops empty path components rather than rejecting them. Describe those checks here, or enforce the stricter contract in the port.
findings.title: Document resolved cgroup containment, not a ban on symlink components.

findings.body:
**Detect activation links in `.upholds` directories.**

If `desktop.target.upholds/crq-tick.service` points to the declared service, the enablement check skips the directory. The recursive scan reads the service fragment as a declared source and misses the link itself. Discovery can then accept a topology in which systemd keeps restarting the selected service. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/257/systemd.unit.html))

Apply the enablement-directory checks to `.upholds` as well. Refuse the undeclared link without changing how declared `.wants` and `.requires` links are handled.
findings.title: Detect activation links in `.upholds` directories.
